text: In the book's point-set topology, a topological space X is defined to be compact when:
choices: X is closed and bounded as a subset of ℝⁿ
every Cauchy sequence in X converges to a point of X
X cannot be written as the disjoint union of two non-empty open sets
every open cover of X has a finite subcover
explanation: The book defines compactness intrinsically: every open cover {U_α} of X admits a finite subcover. 'Closed and bounded' is only the Heine-Borel characterization, special to ℝⁿ; convergence of every Cauchy sequence is completeness (compact vs complete); the disjoint-open-sets condition is connectedness.
